title: Finite surjective descent of truncated nearby-cycle comparison
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), $f:X\to S$ finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring killed by an integer invertible on $S$, and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Let $p:T\to S$ be finite surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For every integer $r$, $P_r(f_T,K_T)$ implies $P_r(f,K)$, with $P_r$ as in [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. The corresponding implication also holds for full $\Psi$-goodness [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].

source.place: Lemma 2.6 and its Cech-nerve proof, pp. 4--5; truncated universal variant by the same bounded-below descent spectral sequence. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Fix $U\to S$, $g:U'\to U$ and a geometric specialization $z'$ of $V_{f_{U'}}$. Work throughout with constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on small etale topoi and the ordinary comparison $\beta_g:v_g^*R\Psi_{f_U}K_U\to R\Psi_{f_{U'}}K_{U'}$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. The tube-comparison lemma identifies its stalk with $u:R\Gamma(M,K_U)\to R\Gamma(N,K_{U'})$. Choose $a$ with $K\in D^{\ge a}$. Exact inverse image and right derived sections give the common lower bound $a$ on both tube complexes. It suffices to prove $H^i\operatorname{Cone}(u)=0$ for $i\le r$ for all these choices: stalk inverse image is exact and the geometric specialization points are conservative on the cohomology module sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: Let $S_0=U_{(f_U(x))}$ and $U_0=U'_{(f_{U'}(x'))}$ for the chosen points. Pull back the given finite cover to $P=T\times_SS_0\to S_0$. Form $P_q=P^{\times_{S_0}(q+1)}$ and $Q_q=U_0\times_{S_0}P_q$. The tube-comparison lemma supplies the augmented diagrams $A_q=R\Gamma(M\times_{S_0}P_q,K)$ and $B_q=R\Gamma(N\times_{U_0}Q_q,K)$, their restriction maps and their decomposition into the local tubes of $f_{P_q}$ and $f_{Q_q}$. Finiteness and surjectivity of these covers follow from the cited arbitrary-base-change stability lemmas; their iterated products are finite by composition. Each is the Cech nerve of that finite surjective map.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: Apply the component lemma with finite morphism $P_q\to S_0$ and base change $U_0\to S_0$. Thus $J_q\to I_q$ is bijective. These are projection-induced maps: for any face or degeneracy, the two composites to $P_q$ agree by the fibre-product equations, so the induced maps on components commute. No separate compatibility theorem or identification of cohomology groups is inferred from the bijection. By the tube-comparison lemma, the column map $u_q:A_q\to B_q$ is the product of the actual ordinary comparison stalks for $Q_q\to P_q$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: Every $P_q$ maps to $T$ by its first cover projection. Consequently $P_r(f_T,K_T)$ applies with preliminary base change $P_q\to T$ and further base change $Q_q\to P_q$. It gives zero cohomology through degree $r$ for each factor cone in Step 3. Finite products of module complexes are termwise finite direct sums: kernels, images and quotients are componentwise, and the cone differential is componentwise. Hence $H^j\operatorname{Cone}(u_q)=0$ for $j\le r$. This conclusion concerns the actual ordinary cochain cones, so no conversion to a truncated-isomorphism assertion, and no edge-surjectivity inference, is needed.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: The projection $M\times_{S_0}P\to M$ is finite surjective by the cited base-change stability of finite and of surjective morphisms. Apply finite-cover hypercohomology descent to $M$ with this cover and to its pullback over $N$, whose $q$-th terms are $M\times_{S_0}P_q$ and $N\times_{S_0}P_q=N\times_{U_0}Q_q$. Both use the same constant ring $\Lambda$ and lower bound $a$. It provides compatible resolved diagrams for $u_q$, quasi-isomorphisms $R\Gamma(M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(A_\bullet)$ and $R\Gamma(N,K)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(B_\bullet)$, and a commuting augmentation square whose top map is $u$. Apply the bounded-below column-cone comparison lemma: its $E_1^{q,j}$ is $H^j\operatorname{Cone}(u_q)$, with $q\ge0$, $j\ge a-1$. For total degree $n\le r$ every term on that diagonal has $j=n-q\le r$ and hence is zero. The lemma's finite convergence gives $H^n\operatorname{Cone}(u)=0$ for $n\le r$. This uses the cone spectral sequence rather than comparing two pages at the truncation edge.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: Since $U$, $g$ and $z'$ were arbitrary, exact stalks and conservativity give the required vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of the comparison cone. The double quantifier in the definition is therefore satisfied, proving $P_r(f,K)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6, printed pp. 4--5, and the explicit bounded-below cone refinement in report.md.

proof.text: For the full assertion, first note directly from the adjoint definition that ordinary comparisons compose: for $V'\xrightarrow{h}V\xrightarrow{g}T$, $\beta_{gh}=\beta_h\circ v_h^*\beta_g$. Indeed, transposing the right-hand composite gives $h^*g^*\varepsilon$ by counit naturality and the adjunction triangle identity, which is the transpose defining $\beta_{gh}$. If $(f_T,K_T)$ is $\Psi$-good, both $\beta_g$ and $\beta_{gh}$ are invertible, so $\beta_h$ is invertible. Hence $(f_V,K_V)$ is $\Psi$-good for every $V\to T$, and $P_r(f_T,K_T)$ holds for every integer $r$. Apply Steps 1--6 for every $r$. In particular the comparison for each $U'\to S$ has an acyclic cone, and is an isomorphism. This is full $\Psi$-goodness for $(f,K)$.

tool_uses.why: Generic scheme-theoretic stability of surjectivity used for the finite Cech covers, independent of the trace/local-term unit.
Only its first, general clause is used: finite morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change and composition. No radicial hypothesis is imposed on the cover.
